text:
Carla - Support: :rotating_light: multiple customers reporting 5xxs and long tails from hosted inference in eu-west-3 (eu3). Error spike started ~2026-11-21T12:04Z. Affected customers: AcmeCorp, FoodCo. Support tickets #5723/#5724. Symptoms: requests hang ~6-12s then 502 or 504, sometimes TCP resets.

Dave - Oncall SRE: Acknowledging, triaging now. Which endpoint are they hitting and any quick repro?

Frank - CSM: Repro from Acme (redacted token):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# -> TCP handshake ok, then after ~8.2s we get HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
# response body: {"error":"upstream connection closed before response"}
```

Ben - NetEng: I'm seeing simultaneous BGP AS path changes from TransitCorp (AS64512) toward our eu3 egress at ~12:05Z. Packet loss spikes on vlan100/egress-0: 2-7% and retransmits jump. Possible asymmetric routing causing some sessions to hit a flaky provider link. Dumping a quick traceroute and tcpdump sample: 
```
traceroute to 198.51.100.10 (198.51.100.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.1.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  198.51.100.10  10.5 ms  10.3 ms  10.4 ms

# tcpdump (partial):
12:05:20.123456 IP our-node > provider-gw: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, length 0
12:05:20.223789 IP provider-gw > our-node: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0  # RSTs seen
```

Ben - NetEng: Also observed mirrored eBGP updates with withdrawn prefixes then reannounce with different next-hop; looks like provider is doing a fast failover and some peers are not converging -> asymmetric path.

Eve - Infra: From the runtime side we're seeing a burst of upstream connection resets to internal model hosts and much higher KV cache miss rates (cold starts). SLOs for 95th/99th token latencies spike. Autoscaler launched new nodes but they didn't help because connections fail at egress.

Dave - Oncall SRE: Confirmed 502 body contains upstream error string "connect timeout / connection reset by peer" in our gateway logs. Example from gateway logs:
```
[2026-11-21T12:06:02Z] gateway-1 | upstream connect error or disconnect/reset by peer
[attempted upstream=10.10.3.42:443]
```

Carla - Support: Customers are escalating; they're asking for ETA and impact scope. They've seen a spike between 12:04-12:20Z. Any mitigation we can offer?

Alice - Routing: I'm opening an emergency ticket with TransitCorp and pushing a policy change to prefer IBGP peer ibgp2 (prefer longer local preference) to steer egress away from the flaky link. If provider confirms blackhole we can prep to move traffic to eu-west-1 for affected customers.

TransitCorp Ops: We've observed a partial egress interface saturation and an automated failover that produced transient withdraws for a subset of prefixes. We're investigating hardware and BGP dampening configs. Working on a mitigation, will confirm within 15m.

Ben - NetEng: Temporary mitigation idea: we can apply a route-map to prefer the backup transit and reduce AS path churn to that transit. Will need approval for a brief flip (risk: some flows will take new path).

Dave - Oncall SRE: Approved. Coordinate with Alice and Ben. I'll prepare the rollback steps and alert routing if anything degrades.

DevOpsBot: Initiating traffic steering canary for 1% of proxy pool -> 10% -> 100% (manual confirm steps). Logs will be tagged with incident_id=inc-20261121-eu3-net.

(12:35Z) Ben - NetEng: Flipped preference to backup transit on canary proxies. Monitoring egress packet loss and gateway 5xx rate.

(12:45Z) Dave - Oncall SRE: Error rate dropping: 5xx from 18% -> 3% over last 5m. Latency tails improving. Client reports coming in.

Frank - CSM: AcmeCorp confirms calls are back to normal for them, FoodCo seeing improvement as well. They asked for root cause timeline and SLA credit discussion.

Alice - Routing: TransitCorp admits automated failover + buggy dampening; they will apply fix and rollback once stable. We're keeping steering in place until they confirm.

Eve - Infra: Raised a follow-up to add detection for asymmetric path-induced RSTs in runtime alerts (new metric: upstream_reset_rate). Also add a runbook step to try alternate egress on next incidents.

Dave - Oncall SRE: Current status: mitigation in place, error rate ~2-3%, customers notified. Postmortem + RCA and SLA assessment to follow. Action items:
- TransitCorp follow-up + ticket id
- Postmortem (owner: Dave)
- Runbook update for asymmetric routing (owner: Eve)
- Customer SLA/credits (owner: Frank)

Carla - Support: Notifying affected customer tickets and marking for priority follow-up. :white_check_mark:

TransitCorp Ops: Confirmed hardware churn fixed at 13:05Z; will monitor for further flaps.

Dave - Oncall SRE: Closing this incident thread; moving to postmortem workspace. Thank you all for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
